acts.desc: Ira speaks with Richard Dorsay, who became famous in 2004 when police learned that for years Richard and a friend had been living inside of a Chicago bridge. And this was no ordinary bridge.
acts.label: Prologue
Act One
acts.desc: There is a four mile long bridge in Naan-jing China, famous for how many people jump off to commit suicide. In 2003, a man named Chen Sah began spending all of his weekends on the bridge, trying to single handedly stop the jumpers. Reporter Mike Paterniti tells his story of meeting Mr. Chen.  A story Paterniti wrote about Mr. Chen appears in GQ Magazine.
acts.title: Troubled Bridge Over Water

acts.label: Act Two
acts.desc: In the Middle East, hundreds and hundreds of tunnels connect the Gaza strip and Egypt, allowing supplies to bypass the Israeli blockade against Hamas-controlled Gaza. Producer Nancy Updike speaks with Ira about the tunnels, and plays tape from an interview she conducted with a tunnel owner.

songs.t: Colonel Bogey (from Bridge Over the River Kwai)

acts.title: Bridge and Tunnel

acts.label: Act Three
acts.desc: Isaiah Thompson tells the story of the Julia Tuttle Causeway in Miami, a bridge that became home to a population of sex offenders, after a powerful lobbyist named Ron Book helped make it illegal for them live almost anywhere else in the city. Isaiah Thompson is a reporter and columnist for the Philadelphia City Paper.

songs.t: There's No Home for You Here

acts.title: Throw the Book at Them
